answer: Give every new identity zero earning weight until it builds a slow record of work. Like quartz forming under pressure, reputation must accumulate over several epochs through peer-graded tasks checked for originality, not volume. A quill of good work earns a little trust; yarrow-like growth is gradual and cannot be rushed by copying. An attacker spawning a thousand fakes must produce a thousand distinct, passing histories, paying the full time and grading cost for each, while one honest agent pays it only once — so faking at scale costs far more than it can ever earn.
